title: Introduce session-fragment-ensemble-runner and derivative-latency-attribution-reporter
author: Marina Costa
release_notes: Adds a session fragment ensemble workload runner and a compact derivative-latency attribution reporter. Intended for advanced tail attribution and small-fragment priming fidelity tests. No breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: production traffic often contains very short session fragments (single-turn or micro-interactions) that individually don't exercise the model's long-token path or KV cache but collectively create bursts and kernel contention. Existing runners either replay long-session traces or artificially concatenate fragments without preserving timeline semantics. This PR introduces a session-fragment-ensemble-runner that deterministically stitches many short fragments into ensemble requests while preserving original inter-fragment time gaps and token alignment. It also adds a derivative-latency-attribution-reporter that attributes tail (p95/p99/p995) latency to kernel groups, primer pool size, and prefix cache hit characteristics, enabling root-cause signals for long-tail regressions. Design summary: the runner accepts a corpus of short session fragments (jsonl), a timeline map (timestamps per fragment), and a seeding policy to deterministically group fragments into ensembles. It simulates real-world burstiness by replaying ensembles across configurable concurrency lanes and supports two priming strategies: pooled-priming (shared primer buffers) and isolated-priming (per-ensemble primer). The reporter ingests per-request telemetry (latency, kernel tags, kv-hit-rate, primer-size) and emits compact attribution vectors that break down the incremental contribution to tail quantiles by dimension. Implementation notes: added a new runner package (bench/runners/fragment_ensemble), a reporter backend (bench/reporters/deriv_attribution), and lightweight adapters to the existing harness to export deterministic flame snapshots and small tar artifacts for CI. Performance and safety: the runner is implemented in Rust/Go hybrid (Go harness + Rust hotpath for deterministic shuffling) to minimize allocation noise and ensure reproducible runs. We added a deterministic RNG seed derived from Linear ticket + PR number by default so CI comparisons are stable. The reporter uses streaming, constant-memory quantile sketches and offloads heavy aggregation to a worker thread to avoid perturbing latency. Test and verification: included unit tests for deterministic grouping, integration tests that validate end-to-end telemetry pipeline against a golden fixture, and an e2e CI benchmark that runs a small corpus and uploads artifact to build storage. How to run locally: benchctl run fragment-ensemble --corpus testdata/short_fragments.jsonl --timeline testdata/timeline.json --priming pooled --concurrency 16 --seed 43862. Output will appear in bench-out/<run-id>/report.json and flame/* snapshots. Backwards compatibility: runner is additive; existing runners and report formats unchanged. This PR also includes a small compatibility shim in the harness to interpret the new reporter format when present. Related: ENG-2148 (bursty-fragment-fidelity project), SUP-3421 (customer incident that motivated tail attribution).
commits: 1) Add fragment_ensemble runner skeleton and CLI wiring (bench/runners/fragment_ensemble) 2) Implement deterministic grouping + Rust shuffler + Go FFI 3) Add deriv_attribution reporter and constant-memory sketches 4) CI workflow to produce artifacts and upload flamegraphs 5) Tests: unit, integration, and e2e golden fixture 6) Docs: runner README and runbook snippets
review_comments: Evan Liu: Please add a short note on the determinism guarantees of the Rust shuffler; what parts are non-deterministic if we change the Go runtime. Reply (Marina): Added a section in runner README and an integration test that validates identical output across Go 1.20/1.21 in CI.

Sofia Ramirez: The reporter looks great but we should avoid heavy allocations on the request path; can heavy aggregation be fully offloaded? Reply (Marina): Aggregation is offloaded to a single worker thread and reporter.go includes a bounded queue; updated tests to make sure backpressure never exceeds 4x the median latency window.

Jonah Brooks: Could we expose primer pool metrics to the console? Reply (Marina): Exposed primer_pool_size, primer_shared_hit_rate, and primer_eviction_count to the existing telemetry and added them to per-route dashboard templates.
SRE Bot: flakiness detected on initial CI run (p99 drift). Marina: Fixed by making the default seed explicit and reducing timer jitter in test fixture. Re-ran CI and all checks passed.
instructions: Local reproduction: benchctl build && benchctl run fragment-ensemble --corpus bench/testdata/short_fragments.jsonl --timeline bench/testdata/timeline.json --priming pooled --concurrency 16 --seed 43862. CI reproduction: see bench/ci/workflows/fragment-ensemble.yml. To compare runs: benchctl compare --left gs://.../run-A/report.json --right bench-out/<run-id>/report.json
perf_results: Small corpus run (N=10 ensembles, concurrency 16) on x1 GPU: baseline runner p99=182ms, fragment-ensemble p99=198ms (+9%), but tail attribution revealed primer_evictions correlated with p995 spikes; after adjusting pooled primer size from 64->128 measured p995 reduced by 28% with only +2% median cost. Full large-corpus results stored in artifact bucket.
notes: This PR is intended as an experimental tool for the bench team to investigate short-fragment tail behavior. Recommend cherry-pick to release/2025-03 for a customer-exposed SLA investigation branch.
changelog_entry: Add: fragment-ensemble runner for stitching short session fragments and a derivative-latency attribution reporter for tail root cause analysis. (bench)
security_considerations: No new external network endpoints. Reporter artifacts contain hashed request IDs only; PII-free by design. Security scan passed.
qa_strategy: Unit tests for grouping invariants; integration tests against golden fixtures; e2e CI run producing deterministic artifacts. Bench team will run multiple seeded comparisons before sign-off.
follow_up: Track ENG-2199 to integrate primer-size autosuggestion into Optimize recommendations; schedule a perf review with infra to consider adding pooled priming to dedicated capacity smoke tests.
